paragraphs.text: Mood Swings is a trading card game developed by Magic: The Gathering Head Designer Mark Rosewater and published by Wizards of the Coast . It was released on June 1, 2026, through the Secret Lair Chaos Vault . Mood Swings was designed to be less complex and more accessible than Magic . It contains several mechanical and creative nods to Magic , including the use of the color pie and of Magic art .

Mood Swings is a light strategy trading card game for two to four people. It can be played out of the box, with no deck building required. Players draw from a single shared deck. During each round, players play one card each in turn order, then scoring occurs. Once a player has won three rounds, they win the game. Similar to Magic , most cards contain special effects that add complexity and alter the rules of the game. A two-person game lasts five to ten minutes.

The First Edition of Mood Swings features randomized deck contents, allowing for optional deck customization by trading with other players. In total, Mood Swings features 133 cards (48 commons, 40 uncommons, 30 rares, 15 mythic rares) . Each box includes 45 of those 133 cards (23 commons, 14 uncommons, 6 rares, 2 mythic rares) . Decks aren't sold with duplicate cards, but a player can customize their deck by adding duplicates without issue.
Mood Swings was heavily influenced by Magic , due in no small part to being designed by Mark Rosewater, Magic' s Head Designer. Similarities include:
It uses the Magic color pie as a mechanical foundation and contains several mechanical nods to Magic .
The card back incorporates the color pie.
The First Edition cards use sketches of Magic art to convey their corresponding emotions.
The Mood Swings logo uses the “M” and “g” of the original Magic logo.
It uses the same four rarities as Magic : common, uncommon, rare, and mythic rare.
The rules text and information below the text box are structured similarly to that of Magic .

Additionally, the first edition in specific is being distributed through the Secret Lair Chaos Vault (a direct-to-consumer store that most frequently sells Magic cards) and, like Magic sets beginning with Innistrad Remastered , features a headliner card: a special version of Love with art by Mark Rosewater. Only 500 of these headliners exist, though they are not serialized . Every copy has been signed and doodled on by Mark Rosewater, and he additionally wrote silly messages on 50 of them.
The information below the text box uses templating that closely matches the M15 frame .
A headliner Love featuring a message from Mark Rosewater.
The Magic card Blackmail ( Onslaught ) was a direct copy of a Mood Swings card. That card, Paranoia, went on to change before Mood Swings was printed.

Rosewater came up with the idea for Mood Swings in 1998 . He was motivated to create a trading card game that didn't follow many of the conventions of a traditional trading card game. He thought he had succeeded, but the problem was that it didn't fit neatly into any box of what Wizards did. He had been trying to get published ever since. For twenty-eight years, Rosewater's wife Lora was his main playtester .

A trademark for Mood Swing was filed by Wizards of the Coast on October 13, 2025. For the final design, Rosewater was assisted by play designer Corey Bowen , editor Michael Zhang , and copy writer Ari Zirulnik . Matt Danner and Ari Zirulnik were in charge of choosing the art. By choosing black and white art, they aimed to capture the vibe of a behind-the-scenes prototype.
The First Edition is being sold exclusively through Secret Lair . Future versions existing depend on how the first edition does.
On June 14, 2026, Scryfall launched Moodfall , a spin-off section of their website for Mood Swings cards.
